method: Structured JSON from the Gemini API, instructed by docs/PROJECT_VISION.md@main blob fe2f414774b7. Every cited URL was fetched; dead links and pages that never mention the character were removed, and feats, results, conditions and campaign tags that lost their source were moved to unknowns. All records provisional. Reviewed by Claude (scheduled independent review) on 2026-11-13: sources opened, claims corrected.

characters.continuity: DC Comics New 52 / DC Rebirth (Prime Earth): Wrath of the First Lantern through Hal Jordan and the Green Lantern Corps
characters.summary: Thaal Sinestro let the fear entity Parallax possess him while keeping control of his body, first to fight the First Lantern Volthoom and again in DC Rebirth. As Parallax's host he gains physical and metaphysical power, reality-altering abilities and a greatly amplified yellow ring, which he used to kill almost all of the Guardians of the Universe.

mechanisms: Personal force field from his yellow power ring

weaknesses: Separation from the Parallax entity
His Parallax-boosted power drops when the fear sources feeding it are cut off: in DC Rebirth it fell after Soranik Natu freed the people powering Warworld's Fear Engine
limitations: His yellow power ring must be recharged regularly from a lantern-shaped power battery
characters.formDifferences: Adds the power of the Parallax entity to Sinestro's yellow power ring: as host he gains physical and metaphysical powers, reality-altering abilities and a greatly amplified ring.

sources.supports: Sinestro hosting Parallax to fight Volthoom, killing the Guardians, DC Rebirth Parallax power boost and defeat on Warworld; yellow ring flight, force field and recharge requirement.
Sinestro bonding with Parallax after Korugar's destruction and killing every Guardian but Sayd and Ganthet.
Sinestro letting Parallax possess him while keeping control, the failed attempt against Volthoom, the Guardians' deaths, and the DC Rebirth defeat by Hal Jordan.

feats.claim: While bonded to Parallax, killed every Guardian of the Universe except Sayd and Ganthet
feats.citation: Wrath of the First Lantern aftermath (issue not named in the source)

notableResults.citation: Wrath of the First Lantern (issue not named in the source)
notableResults.note: Sinestro let Parallax possess him to fight Volthoom, but the attempt failed; Volthoom was defeated only when Hal Jordan returned as a Black Lantern and summoned Nekron.

notableResults.citation: DC Rebirth, Warworld (issue not named in the source)
notableResults.note: Sinestro boosted his Parallax power to 'one thousand percent' when Jordan invaded Warworld, but his power dropped after Soranik Natu freed the people powering the Fear Engine, and Jordan destroyed Warworld.

conditional.ability: Reality-altering abilities and a greatly amplified ring

campaignTags.claim: His yellow power ring grants him flight and the ability to survive in any environment

unknowns: Exact limits of reality-warping while bonded to Parallax.

Removed by review (not supported by the sources opened): defense: Fear-based invulnerability; defense: Regeneration; weakness: Willpower concentration by multiple ring-wielders; limitation: Vulnerable to combined willpower of multiple Green Lanterns; feat: Imprisoned the Guardians of the Universe (the sources say he killed them); result: Hal Jordan loss in Green Lantern (vol. 4) #25 (that issue is not this form; the sourced Hal Jordan loss is the DC Rebirth Warworld fight); tag: mind-control (inducing terror is not mind control).
The cited page dc.fandom.com/wiki/Thaal_Sinestro_(New_Universe) could not be opened (no such New Universe page found); replaced by the Prime Earth page.

characters.continuity: DC Comics New Earth (Post-Crisis): Blackest Night (2009-2010)
characters.summary: During Blackest Night, after Nekron killed Sinestro, the White Entity revived him and bonded with him, making him the first White Lantern. With its life-powered energy he wiped out swarms of Black Lanterns, but he could not fully control the Entity's power and Nekron separated them. (A later New 52 attempt to take Kyle Rayner's white ring failed: the ring rejected him.)

techniques: Life-powered energy that destroys Black Lanterns

mechanisms: Bonded to the White Entity, he seemed to survive a fatal wound, recovering within minutes

weaknesses: The White Entity can be separated from him: Nekron did so
limitations: Could not fully control the White Entity's power
The form was brief: he was discharged after Nekron removed the Entity from him
characters.formDifferences: Instead of his yellow fear ring, Sinestro is bonded to the White Entity (the Life Entity) and wields its white light, powered by life itself, rather than fear.

sources.supports: Nekron killing Sinestro, the White Entity reviving him, his inability to fully control its power, Nekron separating them, and the New 52 white ring rejecting him.
Sinestro as the first White Lantern: wiping out swarms of Black Lanterns, surviving a fatal wound, Nekron separating him from the Entity, and white light constructs powered by life.

feats.claim: As the first White Lantern, wiped out swarms of Black Lanterns with ease
feats.citation: Blackest Night (issue not named in the source)

notableResults.citation: Blackest Night (issue not named in the source)
notableResults.note: Nekron separated Sinestro from the White Entity; Hal Jordan then used the Entity's power against Nekron.

conditional.ability: White light constructs and life-powered energy
conditional.dependsOn: Being bonded to the White Entity

unknowns: Whether he flew under the White Entity's power is not stated by the sources opened.

Removed by review (not supported by the sources opened): technique: Energy blasts; defense: White light energy shields; weakness: Emotional instability disrupts white light connection; limitation: White Lantern rings have limited charge; feat: Created life on a cosmic scale; result: win vs The First Lantern (Volthoom) in Green Lantern (vol. 5) #20 (the white ring rejected him in that arc); tag: flight; tag: healing (Hal Jordan, not Sinestro, used the Entity to restore the dead).

Continuity corrected from New 52 to Blackest Night (New Earth); the cited page dc.fandom.com/wiki/Thaal_Sinestro_(New_Universe) could not be opened and the New Earth page failed to load, so a Wikipedia mirror of the White Lantern Corps article was used instead.

characters.continuity: DC Comics New Earth (Post-Crisis) incarnations of Cyrus Gold
characters.summary: Solomon Grundy is the undead, swamp-born revenant of Cyrus Gold, with superhuman strength and stamina, near-invulnerability and fast regeneration. He is always reborn after being destroyed, and each incarnation differs in strength and intelligence. He fights with brute physical force.

techniques: Detached limbs that keep fighting independently

mechanisms: Impervious to bullets, fire and extreme cold
Radically fast regeneration in Slaughter Swamp, reattaching severed limbs within seconds
Survives without food, water or oxygen

weaknesses: Below-average intellect makes him easy to fool and manipulate
Can be blinded (Batman blinded him with mace)
limitations: Strength and intelligence vary by incarnation, depending on how he was destroyed
Low intelligence makes him susceptible to trickery

sources.supports: Superhuman strength and stamina, near-invulnerability, healing factor and recurring resurrection, immunity to fire and cold, variation between incarnations, and named defeats.
New Earth powers (durability, regeneration, removable limbs, resurrection), diminished intellect, and named New Earth fights.

feats.claim: His detached arms moved independently and helped defeat Amazo
feats.citation: issue not named in the source

feats.citation: issue not named in the source

notableResults.citation: Green Arrow (vol. 3) #18
notableResults.note: Green Arrow killed him by choking him with a broken bowstring (he later returned).

notableResults.citation: Infinite Crisis #7
notableResults.note: Superboy-Prime's heat vision destroyed that incarnation during the Battle of Metropolis.

notableResults.citation: issue not named in the source
notableResults.note: Grundy broke Killer Croc's jaw.

notableResults.citation: Superman/Batman #3
notableResults.note: While mind-controlled by Gorilla Grodd, he attacked Batman and Superman; Batman stopped him.

Removed by review (not supported by the sources opened): technique: Environment destruction; technique: Grappling; defense: Insensitivity to pain; weakness: Vulnerable to fire and magical attacks (contradicted: Wikipedia says he is unaffected by fire and nearly invulnerable to magical attacks); feat: Stalemated Superman in Superman: Man of Steel #29; result: loss to Superman in that issue; tag: giant-sized (no documented size).

characters.summary: Princess Koriand'r of Tamaran constantly absorbs ultraviolet radiation and converts it to energy, giving her supersonic flight, superhuman strength and durability. She fights with starbolts of concentrated solar energy and hand-to-hand skills learned from the Warlords of Okaara.

techniques: Omni-directional release of all stored energy

weaknesses: Left weakened after releasing her stored energy in an omni-directional burst
limitations: Needs food, drink, breath and sleep like others when her stored UV energy runs low

sources.supports: Tamaranean UV absorption, supersonic flight, strength and durability, starbolts, Okaaran combat training, weakness after an omni-directional burst, and the Infinite Crisis fight with Alexander Luthor Jr.
Starbolt and full-energy release details, absorbing Kryptonians' solar radiation, interstellar flight, telepathic immunity, combat training, and the fight with Komand'r.

feats.claim: Absorbed the solar radiation of Kryptonians, weakening them
Can release all her stored energy as a large area blast believed to be as hot as the sun
Has flown light years in short periods

notableResults.citation: issue not named in the source
notableResults.note: Komand'r struck her down with a stronger starbolt and had her restrained for execution; Koriand'r escaped.

notableResults.citation: Infinite Crisis (issue not named in the source)
notableResults.note: She was presumed dead after the fight but survived and was teleported to another planet.

campaignTags.claim: Her Tamaranean body converts absorbed UV energy into supersonic flight, crossing several solar systems in minutes

unknowns: Exact maximum speed in deep space.

Removed by review (not supported by the sources opened): defense: Agility and evasion; weakness: Emotional volatility affects starbolt output; limitation: Depleted of powers if kept in total darkness; feat: Starbolts staggering armored opponents and damaging starships (Teen Titans (vol. 3) #1); result: inconclusive vs Red Hood in Red Hood and the Outlaws #1 (also a New 52 story, not New Earth).

characters.continuity: Milestone Comics Dakotaverse (Static, 1993) and its continuation in the DC Universe after Final Crisis (pre-Flashpoint)
characters.summary: Virgil Hawkins is a Bang Baby whose body generates electromagnetic energy. He fights with electric and magnetic force bolts, ball lightning, force fields and magnetized objects, uses his science knowledge tactically, and flies on a hoverdisc he built.
weaknesses: Insulators such as wood, rubber, cloth and plastic are largely immune to his powers
An outside force can steal his powers (e.g. the electrokinetic Prometheus)
Electric Bang Babies can hurt him even though he is normally immune to high voltage
limitations: Heavy power use causes sudden fatigue, and he must recharge from an electrical source if he cannot rest

sources.supports: Electromagnetic powers, stopping bullets, resisting the Anti-Life Equation, insulator weakness, fatigue and recharging, continuities, and the Holocaust and Hotstreak fights.
Detailed electromagnetic powers, hoverdisc, insulator and power-absorption weaknesses, and named fights (Hotstreak, Holocaust, Rumble).

feats.claim: Resisted Darkseid's Anti-Life Equation through his bioelectric field
Redirected Kryptonite radiation at an enemy

characters.summary: Conner Kent (Kon-El) is a human-Kryptonian clone created by Project Cadmus. He originally simulated Superman's powers with tactile telekinesis, a field around his body that lets him manipulate what he touches, and later gained Kryptonian powers such as heat vision and super-breath. He fights with raw strength and telekinetic tricks.
weaknesses: Powers depend on yellow solar radiation; red-sun radiation affects him, though less severely than full Kryptonians
Arrogance has led to defeats in stressful situations, including against General Zod
limitations: Absorbs less solar energy than Superman, so overexerting his powers can be fatal

sources.supports: Clone origin, tactile telekinesis through touch, later Kryptonian powers, and death fighting Superboy-Prime in Infinite Crisis.
New Earth powers and weaknesses, notable feats and named fights.

characters.summary: Kara Zor-El is a Kryptonian whose body absorbs and stores yellow sun radiation, giving her superhuman strength, speed, invulnerability, flight, heat vision and super-breath. She fights with brute force, heat vision and hand-to-hand skills, and learned to vibrate intangibly from the Flash.
weaknesses: Kryptonite (Gold Kryptonite stripped her powers in her fight with Reactron)
Red solar radiation (she was badly injured in a red-sun environment)
limitations: Powers are fuelled by absorbed and stored yellow sun radiation

characters.continuity: DC Comics New 52 (Prime Earth): Supergirl (vol. 6) #26-33 and Red Lanterns #28-32
characters.summary: After a fight with Lobo unleashed Kara's long-repressed fury, a red power ring found her. Driven insane by rage, she attacked everyone in her way in space until Hal Jordan took her to Ysmault, where the Blood Ocean restored her sanity; she then served in Guy Gardner's Red Lantern Corps. She fights with Kryptonian power plus the ring's corrosive plasma-like blood.

techniques: Corrosive, flammable plasma-like blood expelled from the mouth (Red Lantern ring power)

mechanisms: Red ring lets its wearer survive in deep space

weaknesses: Removal of the Red Lantern ring causes rapid death for standard users (Kara survived it thanks to her healing factor / the Sun restarting her heart)
Blue Lantern light can counter Red Lantern rage (Hal Jordan overcame a red ring's influence with Blue Lantern aid)
limitations: Rage-fuelled state left her barely coherent and attacking everyone in her way until the Blood Ocean of Ysmault restored her sanity
characters.formDifferences: Adds a Red Lantern ring to her Kryptonian powers: the ring fuels her with rage, replaces her circulatory system and gives her corrosive plasma-like blood.

sources.supports: Mirror of the Wikipedia article: the red ring attaching to her after Lobo, her rage-driven rampage, Guy Gardner restoring her sanity, and her discharge from the Corps.
Red Lantern ring acquisition (Supergirl (vol. 6) #26-29), the Blood Ocean (Green Lantern (vol. 5) #28), Red Lanterns service (#28-32) and her removing the ring (Supergirl (vol. 6) #33).
Red Lantern ring powers (light-speed flight, deep-space survival, corrosive plasma-like blood), death on ring removal with Supergirl as the exception, and Blue Lantern aid against red rage.

conditional.ability: Corrosive plasma-like blood that can destroy other Lanterns' constructs and auras

Red Lantern power rings grant the ability to fly at light speed and survive in deep space

unknowns: Long-term psychological toll of sustained Red Lantern ring usage.
Her fight with the last Worldkiller (Supergirl (vol. 6) #33) was won after she removed the ring, so it is not recorded as a result for this form.

Removed by review (not supported by the sources opened): technique: Energy projection; defense: Red Lantern energy shields; feat: Obliterated a starship fleet (Supergirl (vol. 6) #31; the sources say only that she fought the Diasporans and Atrocitus' splinter cell alongside the Red Lanterns); result: win vs Atrocitus in Red Lanterns #29.
The cited page dc.fandom.com/wiki/Kara_Zor-El_(New_Universe) does not exist under that name; the Prime Earth page was used.

characters.continuity: DC Comics Kingdom Come (Earth-22, Elseworlds, 1996) and his later Earth-22 appearances
characters.summary: An older Superman from a future where he retired after Magog's acquittal and then returned to re-form the Justice League. Decades under Earth's sun gave him almost complete immunity to kryptonite; only Captain Marvel's magic lightning seemed to harm him. He fights with Kryptonian strength, heat vision and super-breath.
weaknesses: Magic: only Captain Marvel and his magic lightning seemed to harm him
characters.formDifferences: Older, grayer Superman whose decades of exposure to Earth's sun gave him almost complete immunity to kryptonite.

sources.supports: Mirror of the Wikipedia Kingdom Come article: retirement and return, the Gulag, the fight with Captain Marvel, and the UN nuclear strike.
Earth-22 Superman's powers, near-immunity to kryptonite, vulnerability to Captain Marvel's magic lightning, surviving the nuclear bomb, and later appearances.

feats.claim: Survived the UN nuclear bomb that killed most superpowered fighters at the Gulag battle, through his invulnerability and being farther from the blast than Captain Marvel

notableResults.citation: Kingdom Come (issue not named in the source)
notableResults.note: They fought at the Gulag while Captain Marvel was under Lex Luthor's control; Superman broke the brainwashing, and no winner is stated. Captain Marvel then sacrificed himself to the nuclear warhead.
